docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
GigaMeter Research Hub

The open-source telemetry research on internet connectivity, network quality, and physical location integrity across GigaMeter installed public facilities.

Spatial Intelligence

Models for entity geofencing, hardware mobility trajectories, and Wi-Fi spatial clustering.

Connectivity & Outages

Advanced telemetry models evaluating network uptime.

Network Diagnostics

NDT7 metric analysis to detect ISP throttling via bufferbloat latency and BBR capacity.

docs.title: Python API Overview
docs.text:
The spatial methodology is implemented in the src.spatial_intelligence package, with data loading in src.utils. This page shows how the pieces fit together. The pages that follow document every public class and function, generated from the code.

Code is imported from the repository root, for example from src.spatial_intelligence.facility_validator import FacilityValidator. Run notebooks and scripts with the repository root as the working directory.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
FacilityValidator runs the whole chain, so most analyses start and end with it:

```python from src.spatial_intelligence.facility_validator import FacilityValidator

validator = FacilityValidator( file_path="data/spatial_confidence_ledger/ALB/ALB_spatial_confidence_ledger_05-08-2026.csv", )

audit = validator.run_national_facility_audit() # one row per facility audit["location_verification_flag"].value_counts()

one = validator.evaluate_facility_location_confidence(audit["school_id_giga"].iloc[0]) one["recommended_action"], one["score_breakdown"] ```

The audit columns are described in Blueprint Section 7. Every row carries methodology_version and config_hash, so results from different settings can be told apart.

Telemetry can come from three sources; give exactly one:

Argument Source telemetry_df A pandas DataFrame already in memory file_path A .csv or .parquet ledger query_name and query_params A SQL template under sql/, run against the database configured in .env

Official pins come from the ledger when it has govt_latitude and govt_longitude, otherwise from Delta Sharing with country_iso3. Track 3 needs the pins of every facility in the country, not only those in the telemetry; pass country_iso3="ALB", load_entity_pins=True to load them, or pass a table as entity_pins. validator.entity_pins_source records which was used.

docs.title: Processing Order
docs.text:
Constructing a FacilityValidator runs these steps once. Results are cached, so later calls are cheap.

Step Component What it produces 1 TelemetryLoader Canonical columns, official pins, local time 2 SpatialProfiler (on construction) Hotspot and BSSID mobility tags, fix events 3 MobilityAnalyzer One mobility class per device 4 SpatialProfiler.build_facility_spatial_summary Observation clusters and one anchor per facility 5 FacilityValidator S_raw and the three tracks per facility

The intermediate objects stay available on the validator:

Attribute Contents validator.df The canonical telemetry frame validator.valid_geo_df Rows with Wi-Fi coordinates (the no-IP rule applied) validator.spatial_profiler The SpatialProfiler, with fix_events and build_bssid_profiles() validator.mobility_analyzer The MobilityAnalyzer, with generate_facility_mobility_report() for device classes validator.facility_summary One row per facility from anchor selection validator.config The SpatialConfig used

docs.title: Changing Settings
docs.text:
All numeric settings live in one SpatialConfig. To try a different value, derive a copy and pass it in:

```python from src.spatial_intelligence.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.with_overrides(anchor_eps_m=200.0) validator = FacilityValidator(file_path=..., config=config) ```

The copy is validated when it is created, and its config_hash differs from the default, so its outputs are stamped accordingly. The defaults and their reasons are on the Parameters page.

docs.title: Using the Components Separately
docs.text:
MobilityAnalyzer and SpatialProfiler accept the same data arguments as FacilityValidator and can be used on their own, for example to study devices without scoring facilities:

```python from src.spatial_intelligence.mobility_analyzer import MobilityAnalyzer

mobility = MobilityAnalyzer(file_path=...) devices = mobility.generate_facility_mobility_report() # one row per device ```

Run alone, MobilityAnalyzer measures the geofence audit against each device's dominant cluster, because no facility anchors are known yet.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text: Classes also provide Plotly figures used by the research dashboard. They are listed under Plots on each class page and return a plotly.graph_objects.Figure.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
SpatialConfig holds every numeric setting of the methodology: distances, day counts, score weights and thresholds. It is frozen, so a run cannot change its settings halfway. DEFAULT_CONFIG is the published v0.3 configuration; the value and reason for each setting are on the Parameters page.

```python from src.spatial_intelligence.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

custom = DEFAULT_CONFIG.with_overrides(device_eps_m=200.0, workdays=(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) custom.provenance() # {"methodology_version": "0.3", "config_hash": "..."} ```

with_overrides returns a new config and checks it: contradictory settings, such as verified_max_m not below mismatch_min_m, raise ValueError.

Every output row is stamped with methodology_version and config_hash. Two rows with the same hash were produced with identical settings.

docs.title: Output Values
docs.text:
The string values that appear in outputs. Each is also a constant in the module named, so code can compare against the constant instead of a literal.

Track 1 flags (facility_validator, FLAG_*): VERIFIED_ACCURATE, CAMPUS_DISPERSION, GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH, AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER, UNSTABLE_MOBILE_ONLY, NO_GOVT_PIN_AVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

Recommended actions (facility_validator, ACTION_*): SUBMIT_CORRECTION, FIELD_VERIFY, AWAIT_DATA, NONE.

Track 3 attribution (facility_validator, ATTRIBUTION_*): CONSISTENT, OTHER_ENTITY_NEARBY, UNRESOLVED.

Track 3 pin source (facility_validator, PINS_FROM_*): entity_pins (passed in), delta_sharing (loaded), telemetry_pins (only facilities in the telemetry).

Mobility classes (mobility_analyzer.MOBILITY_CLASSES): STATIONARY, COMMUTER, RELOCATED, HIGH_MOBILITY, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

Geofence reference (mobility_analyzer, REFERENCE_*): facility_anchor, device_dominant_cluster.

Anchor resolution (spatial_profiler, RESOLVED_BY_*): strategy_agreement, single_strategy, ssid_name_match, unresolved, no_cluster.

Strategy fallback reasons (spatial_profiler, FALLBACK_*): no_govt_pin, no_cluster_within_govt_anchor_radius, no_device_classes, no_stationary_evidence.

Their meaning is defined in the Blueprint. Colours used for these values in plots are in src.spatial_intelligence.palette.

docs.title: Data Loading
docs.text:
Every analysis class loads telemetry through TelemetryLoader, so all of them see the same columns. The loader:

  1. reads one source: a DataFrame, a .csv or .parquet file, or a SQL template;
  2. renames known synonyms to the canonical names, for example giga_id_school to school_id_giga;
  3. merges official pins as govt_latitude and govt_longitude when the telemetry does not already have them;
  4. converts UTC timestamps to local time at the facility and adds the operational-hours flags.

It never fills detected_latitude or detected_longitude from IP coordinates in client_info. Rows without a Wi-Fi location keep null coordinates and are dropped later by the spatial classes.

docs.title: Column Contract
docs.text:
Required after canonicalisation:

Column Meaning school_id_giga Facility identifier (giga_id_school is accepted) device_id Device identifier; may be null for older app versions detected_latitude, detected_longitude Google Wi-Fi geolocation result, or null created_timestamp UTC time of the measurement

Added by the loader:

Column Meaning govt_latitude, govt_longitude Official pin, when one is found tz_name IANA time zone of the facility local_created_timestamp, local_date, local_hour, local_day_of_week Local time fields is_weekday Monday to Friday is_operational_hours 08:00:00 to 19:59:59 local time

Optional Wi-Fi columns are renamed when present: detected_bssid to detected_wifi_bssid, detected_ssid to detected_wifi_ssid, and detected_wifi_signal to wifi_signal_dbm.

docs.title: MobilityAnalyzer(telemetry_df=None, *, file_path=None, query_name=None, query_params=None, country_iso3=None, schools_df=None, timestamp_col='created_timestamp', db=None, delta_store=None, geofence_radius_m=None, strategy=None, facility_summary=None, config=DEFAULT_CONFIG, fix_event_rows=None)
docs.text:
Pillar 1 Mobility Engine for GigaMeter telemetry.

Each device is clustered on its own non-carried fix events. A cluster is supported when it spans at least min_cluster_device_days days; unsupported clusters count as noise.

  • STATIONARY: one supported cluster and noise share within max_noise_share.
  • COMMUTER: two or more supported clusters, with at least commuter_min_alternations switches between them over time.
  • RELOCATED: two or more supported clusters visited in sequence.
  • HIGH_MOBILITY: no supported cluster, or too much noise.
  • INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: fewer than device_min_samples fix events or fewer than min_cluster_device_days days, so no cluster could be supported. Checked first.

Geofence compliance is an audit, not an input to the class. It is measured against the facility anchor when facility_summary is given, otherwise against the device's dominant cluster.

Spatial analytics engine for GigaMeter telemetry.

On load, every row is tagged with:

  • is_hotspot_ssid: the SSID matches config.hotspot_ssid_pattern.
  • is_laa_bssid: the BSSID is a locally administered MAC (evidence only).

  • is_mobile_hotspot: is_hotspot_ssid or is_mobile_bssid.

build_facility_spatial_summary then clusters each facility's anchor-window fix events and selects one anchor cluster.

docs.title: build_facility_spatial_summary(device_events=None)
docs.text:
Cluster each facility's anchor-window fix events and pick its anchor.

Anchor-window events are non-carried fix events inside operational hours on configured workdays, from all devices, with or without a BSSID. DBSCAN uses anchor_eps_m and a minimum of one event, so every event belongs to a cluster and support decides which clusters count. Each configured strategy proposes one cluster; agreement, then a registry-name match, resolves the anchor. A cluster name-matches when SSIDs matching the registry name are seen on at least min_support_device_days of its device-days.

docs.title: Research Log
docs.text:
This page records how the spatial methodology changed between versions and why. The methodology pages (Blueprint, the three pillar pages, and Parameters) always describe the current version on their own; this log is the place for history.

Concrete facilities that motivated a change are described, anonymised, in Worked Examples.

docs.title: v0.3
docs.text: Status: frozen after replay validation (see Validation).

docs.title: Findings That Motivated v0.3
docs.text:
Replaying v0.2 on one country ledger (summer 2026, about 9,200 rows from 245 devices) showed:

  • Repeated coordinates are the norm. 72% of rows carry exactly the same (lat, lon, accuracy) as the previous row from the same device. The median gap between such repeats is about 4 hours 40 minutes, and 19% repeat after more than a day.
  • Coordinates can be carried across networks. 66% of changes in associated BSSID keep the previous row's exact coordinates. In one case a home network carried the school's coordinates from about 12 hours earlier, 3 km away.
  • Cluster labels were treated as meaningful. DBSCAN cluster 0 (the first cluster in time) was used as the primary cluster.
  • Rows without a BSSID were averaged across locations. When that group had the most scans, every row for the facility was averaged, placing the facility between real locations.
  • The Track 1 cascade had a gap. Any score from 50 to below 70 produced MINOR_DISCREPANCY, including offsets of 15–38 km.
  • Mobility depended on the facility centroid. A wrong centroid made every device fail the geofence and fall into HIGH_MOBILITY.

docs.text: Change Reason Fix events replace rows as the evidence unit Repeated and carried coordinates inflated density and made fixed routers look mobile Device mobility runs before facility selection and does not use the facility centroid A wrong centroid misclassified every device; it also made STATIONARY_FIRST impossible INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE device class for devices with fewer than device_min_samples fix events or fix events on a single day The first replay of the new rules put 44 devices in HIGH_MOBILITY, against 20 in v0.2. 35 of them had one day with one or two fix events and no movement at all. They could not form a supported cluster, so they fell through to the "no supported cluster" rule. The class scores like HIGH_MOBILITY, so no facility output changed Facility anchor is one observation cluster; no averaging across clusters Averages across locations produced points where no device had been Two strategies always run, with agreement and a registry-name tie-break Strategy fallback was silent and the reported strategy was the requested one A cluster name-matches only when the facility's SSID is seen there on at least min_support_device_days device-days In the commuter example a single non-carried reading of the school SSID sat in the home cluster, so both candidates matched and the tie-break could not decide Track 1 flag is set by distance; confidence is a separate tier with a recommended action Low and medium scores hid large offsets Track 2 split measured between supported clusters Stray readings and the no-BSSID group produced false splits Track 3 (entity attribution) added No way to tell a wrong pin from telemetry recorded somewhere else All settings in one versioned config Constants were duplicated, and some existed only in the docs

All fixed in v0.3:

  • TelemetryLoader lost tz_name under pandas 3, because groupby(...).apply no longer returns the grouping column. The time zone is now mapped per facility.
  • The SQL app-version filter compared strings, so 2.0.10 sorted below 2.0.2. Versions are now compared as integer arrays.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
v0.2 and v0.3 were replayed on the same ledger with scripts/replay_versions.py. The v0.2 side is the last v0.2 commit, 66d9596. The ledger is the one behind the findings above: one country, June to mid-August 2026, 9,189 rows, 245 devices, 165 facilities, 541 BSSIDs, official pins from Delta Sharing.

Track 1 flags:

Flag v0.2 v0.3 VERIFIED_ACCURATE 47 61 CAMPUS_DISPERSION 11 7 GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH 76 80 MINOR_DISCREPANCY 25 retired AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER — 5 UNSTABLE_MOBILE_ONLY 0 1 INSUFFICIENT_DATA 6 11

Flag transitions (rows are v0.2, columns are v0.3):

126 of 165 facilities keep their flag. The median change in distance to the pin is 0 m, and 12 facilities move by more than 1 km. The 25 retired MINOR_DISCREPANCY facilities now get a distance band: 9 of them are mismatches of more than 500 m that v0.2 had shown under its mildest flag.

Confidence and actions: 129 facilities are HIGH, 24 MEDIUM and 12 LOW. Recommended actions are FIELD_VERIFY for 84, NONE for 61, AWAIT_DATA for 13 and SUBMIT_CORRECTION for 7. 70 of the 80 mismatches are seen by a single device, which cannot show whether the pin or the installation is wrong, so they go to field verification.

Device classes:

v0.2 \ v0.3 STATIONARY COMMUTER RELOCATED HIGH_MOBILITY INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE v0.2 total STATIONARY 144 0 0 0 33 177 COMMUTER 1 34 2 2 0 39 RELOCATED 2 0 7 0 0 9 HIGH_MOBILITY 5 5 1 1 8 20 v0.3 total 152 39 10 3 41 245

The 33 devices v0.2 called STATIONARY had too little data to be called anything: v0.2 passed them because one or two readings trivially sit inside the geofence. Only 3 devices remain HIGH_MOBILITY.

Hotspot and BSSID mobility: 1,504 of the 9,189 rows are carried fixes. Excluding them from the BSSID mobility test takes the number of mobile BSSIDs from 55 to 7: 49 lose the tag and 1 gains it. Hotspot-tagged rows fall from 2,599 to 693, and hotspot-tagged BSSIDs from 204 to 132; the remaining tags come mostly from hotspot network names.

Worked examples: The three Worked Examples were replayed. Their v0.2 outputs match the earlier analysis exactly, and their v0.3 outputs match the design, with one difference: Example B was expected to have its confidence limited by its 130 m accuracy, but other factors put it in the HIGH tier. Its action is still FIELD_VERIFY.

Second extract and other countries: A later extract of the same country (8,395 rows, 186 devices, 162 facilities) gives the same picture: 118 of 162 facilities keep their flag, HIGH_MOBILITY falls from 13 to 3 devices, and hotspot-tagged rows fall from 2,430 to 385. Ledgers from three more countries (about 1,700 facilities in total) were run through v0.3 alone. Every facility in all four ledgers satisfies the Track 1 distance bands, the support and anchor rules, the confidence tiers and the SUBMIT_CORRECTION conditions. Two random facilities per flag and country were also reviewed by hand.

docs.title: Findings Recorded for Later Versions
docs.text:
• Country-wide pin offset. In one country, 410 of 805 facilities are CAMPUS_DISPERSION. The anchors sit a median of about 226 m from their pins, mostly in the same direction: the median facility pin is about 211 m west and 29 m south of its anchor. Removing that shared shift leaves a median residual of 64 m. The other three countries show no shared shift, with medians under 5 m. This points to a registry-wide error such as a datum or projection problem, not to dispersed campuses. v0.3 reports it facility by facility (Blueprint Section 9); a registry-level check is a candidate for a later version.
  • Missing device identifiers. In one country about three quarters of rows have no device_id, from older app versions. These rows still support facility clusters but cannot be classified by device, so distinct_devices can be 0 for a supported facility.

docs.title: v0.2
docs.text: Introduced the Two-Track Engine. Earlier iterations used a single-flag cascade in which a hardware anomaly, for example a laptop carried 200 km, replaced the location answer even when the main cluster matched the government pin. v0.2 split the output into Track 1 (location truth, from the unpenalized score S_raw) and Track 2 (hardware integrity, S_raw x P_coherence), added the BSSID Coherence Penalty, the consumer-hotspot regex, and the BSSID drift check, and introduced configurable cluster-resolution strategies.

docs.title: Geofencing: Technical Blueprint & Research Methodology
docs.text:
Version: v0.3

Status: Frozen

Maturity: Validated on Replay

Scope

This page describes the v0.3 methodology, which the modules under src/spatial_intelligence/ implement. Numeric settings are listed on the Parameters page; values marked calibrate were checked on replay but rest on limited data. Replay results and the history of the method are recorded in the Research Log.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text: The primary objective of this framework is to replace static, self-reported administrative registries with spatially verified, crowdsourced field telemetry. By capturing Wi-Fi geolocation results and active speedtests via the GigaMeter application, the system calculates location truth, evaluates device mobility trajectories, cross-validates official government records, and checks whether the telemetry is attributable to the registered entity.

docs.title: 1.1 The 3 Research Pillars
docs.text: Pillar Name Primary Input Data Core Methodologies Primary Output / Operational Value Pillar 1: Entity Geofencing & Mobility Device fix events, device_id, local timestamps Per-device DBSCAN on fix events, support by device-days, cluster transitions Mobility classification (STATIONARY, COMMUTER, RELOCATED, HIGH_MOBILITY, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) with a separate evidence level. Pillar 2: Geolocation Quality & Confidence Google API resolved lat/lon, accuracy, BSSIDs, SSIDs Fix events, BSSID mobility test, facility observation clusters, inverse-variance centroids, 5-factor score, BSSID Coherence Penalty Facility anchor cluster, unpenalized location score (S_raw), mobile hotspot tags, hardware health score. Pillar 3: Government Data Validation Anchor centroid, official registry pins, registry names Haversine displacement (D_govt), strategy agreement, Three-Track Engine Decoupled flags: location truth with confidence tier, hardware anomaly tags, entity attribution.

docs.title: 1.2 Multi-Track Engine
docs.text:
A facility can be correctly located while its monitoring hardware is unreliable, and the reverse. A single combined flag would hide one answer behind the other, so the engine reports independent tracks. No track's output is folded into another track's flag.

  1. Track 1: Location Truth Engine (Pillar 3): Where is the facility anchor relative to the official pin, and how much evidence supports that answer?
  2. Track 2: Hardware Integrity Engine (Pillars 1 & 2): Are the monitoring devices a trustworthy installation (stationary, fixed infrastructure, no splits)?
  3. Track 3: Entity Attribution Engine (Pillar 3): Is the anchor plausibly the registered entity, rather than another facility or a private location?

Later versions may add tracks.

docs.title: 2. Evidence Unit: Fix Events
docs.text:
Each speedtest triggers a fresh lookup: the client scans the associated and nearby Wi-Fi access points, and the backend resolves that list through the Google Geolocation API into detected_latitude, detected_longitude, and detected_location_accuracy.

Many consecutive rows from one device still carry exactly the same (lat, lon, accuracy). Three situations produce this:

  • Bursts: several tests seconds or minutes apart.
  • Unchanged environment: a later test sees the same access points and Google returns the same answer. This is genuine repeated evidence.
  • Carried fixes: the same coordinates appear under a different associated network, sometimes kilometres from that network's other fixes. The cause is not confirmed (see Known Limitations).

Counting rows overstates evidence, and carried fixes attach coordinates to the wrong network.

Rows are converted to fix events per device, in time order:

  1. Burst collapse: Consecutive rows with the same fix within burst_window_s form one event.
  2. Fresh repeat: The same fix under the same BSSID after a longer gap is a new event. It adds support (another session or day) but the centroid weights each event once, not each row.
  3. Carried fix: Consecutive rows with the same fix form a run; the run's origin network is the first associated BSSID in it. A row whose BSSID differs from its run's origin network is marked fix_carried = True. It is excluded from BSSID mobility tests, BSSID centroids, and cluster support, and remains available to non-spatial analyses. Rows with no associated network are never carried and do not set the origin, because a device switching between cable and Wi-Fi in one place legitimately gets the same answer. Excluding a carried row loses no location: the same coordinates are already counted under the origin network.

Support for a location is counted in distinct device-days of non-carried fix events, then distinct devices, then events.

docs.title: 4.1 Processing Passes
docs.text:
• Pass 1: Input: The device's non-carried fix events, all hours. Weekends are kept because they carry commuting and relocation signal.
  • Pass 2: DBSCAN: Haversine metric on fix events with device_eps_m and device_min_samples (counted in events, not rows).
  • Pass 3: Support: A cluster is supported when it spans at least min_cluster_device_days distinct days. Unsupported clusters are treated as noise.
  • Pass 4: Evidence gate: A device with fewer than device_min_samples fix events, or with fix events on fewer than min_cluster_device_days days, cannot form a supported cluster at all. It is classed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of being called mobile.
  • Pass 5: Classification: Uses the device's own supported clusters and how often the device switches between them. Cluster labels carry no meaning; the dominant cluster is the one with the most support (device-days, then events, then the earliest start), not cluster 0.

A transition is a change of supported cluster between two consecutive fix events of the device, in time order, ignoring noise events. A device that moves once and stays has one transition; a device that goes back and forth has many.

docs.title: 4.2 Classification Rules

Mobility Class Rule Real-World Context STATIONARY Exactly one supported cluster and noise share ≤ max_noise_share Fixed desktop or router-attached device. Mobility class and amount of evidence are separate fields. Each device also reports evidence_device_days, so a stationary device seen on 3 days and one seen on 60 days share a class but not an evidence level.

docs.title: 4.3 Geofence Audit
docs.text:
Geofence compliance is reported per device but never feeds its class. It is the share of the device's fix events within geofence_radius_m of a reference point. reference_source names that point:

  • facility_anchor: the facility's anchor centroid (Section 5), used once the anchor is known.
  • device_dominant_cluster: the centroid of the device's own dominant cluster, used when no anchor is available.
  • Empty when the device has no supported cluster; compliance and displacement are then not computed.

docs.title: 4.4 Device Output
docs.text: Field Meaning mobility_class One of the five classes above. total_scans, carried_scans Telemetry rows with valid coordinates, and how many of them are carried. total_fix_events Non-carried fix events used for clustering. evidence_device_days Distinct local dates with at least one fix event. cluster_count, supported_cluster_count DBSCAN clusters found, and how many are supported. noise_share, cluster_transitions Inputs to the classification rules. dominant_cluster_id, dominant_cluster_device_days, dominant_centroid_lat, dominant_centroid_lon The best-supported cluster and its accuracy-weighted centroid. reference_source, compliance_rate_pct, max_displacement_m, median_displacement_m Geofence audit (Section 4.3). methodology_version, config_hash Provenance of the settings used.

docs.title: 5.1 Data Ingestion Rules
docs.text:
1. No-IP Policy: Rows with null detected_latitude or detected_longitude are dropped. client_info IP coordinates are never used as facility pins.
  2. Anchor Window: Facility clustering uses fix events inside 08:00:00–19:59:59 local time on configured workdays. Device mobility (Layer 1) uses all hours.
  3. Fix Events: As defined in Section 2.

docs.title: 5.2 Hotspot & BSSID Mobility Signals
docs.text:
• SSID regex: A case-insensitive consumer hotspot pattern (hotspot_ssid_pattern, for example iphone, galaxy, hotspot, mifi) sets is_hotspot_ssid.
  • BSSID mobility (is_mobile_bssid): Keep fix events for one BSSID with accuracy ≤ bssid_mobility_accuracy_gate_m, excluding carried fixes. Run DBSCAN with bssid_mobility_eps_m and bssid_mobility_min_samples. The BSSID is mobile when two or more clusters each span at least bssid_mobility_min_cluster_days. A single stray reading cannot mark a fixed router as mobile.
  • Locally administered MAC bit: Recorded as is_laa_bssid. Phone hotspots commonly randomise their MAC, but mesh routers also set this bit, so it is evidence, not a trigger.
  • is_mobile_hotspot = is_hotspot_ssid OR is_mobile_bssid.

docs.title: 5.3 Facility Observation Clusters
docs.text:
The facility is located from clusters of observations, not from BSSIDs. A BSSID can appear at more than one place, and many tests have no associated BSSID at all (wired or unassociated devices), so grouping by BSSID cannot separate locations.

  1. Run DBSCAN (anchor_eps_m, minimum one event) on the facility's anchor-window fix events from all devices, including events without a BSSID. Every event belongs to a cluster; support, not DBSCAN, decides which clusters count.
  2. Each cluster records its BSSIDs, SSIDs, devices, device-days, event count, hotspot share, mean accuracy, and distance to the official pin.
  3. A cluster is supported when it has at least min_support_device_days distinct device-days. Candidates are the supported clusters; when none is supported, all clusters are candidates and the anchor is reported with anchor_supported = false.
  4. Candidates whose hotspot share is at least hotspot_share_min are excluded when a non-hotspot candidate exists.
  5. Anti-blending invariant: a centroid is only ever computed inside one cluster. No facility coordinate is an average across clusters.

docs.title: 5.4 Strategy Candidates & Agreement
docs.text:
Each strategy selects one candidate cluster. Ranking within a strategy is by support (device-days, then devices, then events).

  • GOVT_PROXIMITY_ANCHOR: Highest-support cluster with its centroid within govt_anchor_radius_m of the official pin. Distance to the pin only breaks support ties. Falls back to TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE when the facility has no pin (no_govt_pin) or no cluster is in range (no_cluster_within_govt_anchor_radius).
  • TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE: Highest-support cluster, ignoring the pin.
  • STATIONARY_FIRST: Highest-support cluster when support is counted only from events of STATIONARY devices and the dominant cluster of COMMUTER devices. Falls back to TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE when device classes are not provided (no_device_classes) or no such events exist (no_stationary_evidence).

The default run evaluates GOVT_PROXIMITY_ANCHOR and TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE:

graph TD
    A["Candidates: govt proximity, telemetry dominance"]
    Q{"Same cluster?"}

    TB["Anchor = name-matched cluster<br/>anchor_resolved_by = ssid_name_match"]

Registry name match: The registry name and SSID are lowercased, stripped of diacritics, and cleaned of generic tokens (name_match_generic_tokens, for example shkolla, school, grade labels, band suffixes such as 2.4g). A number written directly before a generic token is dropped with it, so 9-vjeçare and the 2 of 2.4g do not count. An SSID matches when it contains every remaining token of the registry name; a registry name with no remaining token never matches.

A cluster name-matches when matching SSIDs are seen on at least min_support_device_days of its device-days. A single reading of the facility's SSID at a staff member's home therefore does not make the home cluster match. The name match is used only to break a strategy disagreement and is always recorded.

Every facility reports anchor_cluster_id, anchor_bssids, strategy_candidates, candidate_govt_displacement_m, strategy_agreement, anchor_resolved_by, and strategy_fallback_reason. anchor_resolved_by is one of:

Value Meaning strategy_agreement All configured strategies chose the same cluster. single_strategy Only one strategy is configured. ssid_name_match Strategies disagreed; exactly one candidate name-matches. unresolved Strategies disagreed and the name match did not decide. No anchor centroid is reported; candidate distances are. no_cluster The facility has no anchor-window fix events.

docs.title: 5.5 Accuracy-Weighted Centroid
docs.text:
Inside the anchor cluster, each fix event gets one weight:

\[w_i = \frac{1}{\max(A_i, A_{\text{floor}})^2}, \quad \bar{\phi} = \frac{\sum w_i \phi_i}{\sum w_i}, \quad \bar{\lambda} = \frac{\sum w_i \lambda_i}{\sum w_i}\]

Because averaging is confined to one cluster, the planar lat/lon mean is adequate at campus scale.

docs.title: 6.1 Raw Score (S_raw)
docs.text:
Five factors are computed on the anchor cluster, not on all of the facility's telemetry, so evidence from other locations does not raise or lower the anchor's confidence.

\[S_{\text{raw}} = S_{\text{stability}} + S_{\text{consensus}} + S_{\text{bssid}} + S_{\text{depth}} + S_{\text{precision}}\] Component Max v0.3 input S_stability 30 Mobility classes of devices contributing to the anchor cluster S_consensus 25 Max distance between each contributing device's dominant supported cluster centroid (single device: 12.5) S_bssid 20 Non-hotspot BSSIDs in the anchor cluster and their active days S_depth 15 Distinct device-days in the anchor cluster S_precision 10 Mean accuracy of anchor fix events

Breakpoints are on the Parameters page.

Recommended action (recommended_action). Rules are checked in order and the first match wins:

Scoring cluster. S_raw is computed on the anchor cluster. For AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER, which has no anchor, it is computed on the TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE candidate and reported as score_cluster_id.

govt_displacement_m is reported whenever an anchor and a pin exist, whatever the flag. For AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER, candidate_govt_displacement_m gives each candidate's distance instead.

A stationary single-device anchor proves the device does not move, not that it sits in the facility. This is why single-device mismatches route to FIELD_VERIFY.

docs.title: 6.3 Track 2: Hardware Integrity
docs.text:
\[\text{Hardware Health} = S_{\text{raw}} \times P_{\text{coherence}}\]

\(D_{\text{split}}\) is the maximum distance between supported facility clusters. Unsupported stray readings do not contribute.

\[P_{\text{coherence}} = \begin{cases} 1.0, & \text{if } D_{\text{split}} \le \text{coherence\_full\_m} \\[1ex] 1.0 - 0.5 \times \left( \frac{D_{\text{split}} - \text{coherence\_full\_m}}{\text{split\_m} - \text{coherence\_full\_m}} \right), & \text{if } \text{coherence\_full\_m} < D_{\text{split}} \le \text{split\_m} \\[1ex] \text{coherence\_floor}, & \text{if } D_{\text{split}} > \text{split\_m} \end{cases}\] Anomaly Tag Trigger BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT \(D_{\text{split}}\) > split_m HOTSPOT_TETHERED_FACILITY Share of non-carried fix events tagged is_mobile_hotspot ≥ hotspot_share_min COMMUTER_DEVICE At least one contributing device is COMMUTER RELOCATED_DEVICE At least one device is RELOCATED

docs.title: 6.4 Track 3: Entity Attribution
docs.text:
Track 3 never changes the Track 1 flag. Its only interaction with Track 1 is the registry-name tie-break in Section 5.4, which is recorded in anchor_resolved_by.

Field Meaning ssid_name_match Anchor SSIDs match the registered entity name (Section 5.4 rule) nearest_other_entity_id, nearest_other_entity_distance_m Closest official pin of a different entity in the same country table Attribution Flag Trigger CONSISTENT ssid_name_match is true, or this entity's pin is the nearest official pin to the anchor and within mismatch_min_m of it OTHER_ENTITY_NEARBY Not CONSISTENT, and another entity's pin is within other_entity_radius_m of the anchor UNRESOLVED Neither, or the facility has no anchor

The mismatch_min_m condition stops a far-off pin from counting as "nearest" only because no other pin is close.

Track 3 needs the country table of official pins, loaded from the same Delta Sharing source the loader reads (load_entity_pins), or passed in directly. Without it only the pins of facilities in the telemetry are known, and entity_pins_source records which was used. The canonical telemetry frame and its column contract do not change.

docs.title: 8. Data Dictionary Rules
docs.text:
• Measurement Source: source = 'DailyCheckApp'. The app-version filter must compare versions numerically, not as strings.
  • Timezone: UTC created_timestamp is converted to local time before any operational-hours or workday rule.
  • No-IP Policy: Never impute detected_* from client_info. Drop null coordinates before spatial work.
  • Fix Events: All spatial evidence is counted in fix events and device-days, never raw rows.
  • Missing device_id: Older app versions do not send a device identifier. Their rows still count as facility evidence, with all of a facility's unidentified rows on one day treated as one device-day, so support is undercounted rather than inflated. They are not classified in Pillar 1 and do not count towards distinct_devices, which can therefore be 0 for a facility with supported clusters.
  • Missing device_id: Older app versions do not send a device identifier. Their rows still count as facility evidence, treated as one unknown device per day, which can undercount but never inflates support. They are left out of device mobility and out of distinct_devices, so a facility can report many device-days and zero distinct devices.

docs.title: 9. Known Limitations
docs.text:
• No term calendar: School holidays are not modelled. Over a long holiday a staff laptop's home cluster can out-support the facility cluster, which surfaces as a strategy disagreement.
  • Fixed workdays: workdays is one config value, not resolved per country.
  • Carried-fix cause: Each test runs a fresh lookup and a failed lookup is not replaced by an earlier result, yet carried fixes are observed. Candidate causes are a Wi-Fi scan list returned from the operating system's cache (for example after sleep and resume) or caching of lookup results in the backend. Neither is confirmed, and the stored ledger does not include the nearby access-point list needed to tell them apart. The carried-fix rule is inferred from the data and does not depend on the cause. A lookup timestamp in the payload would make it observable; this is not planned for v0.3.
  • Stale but newly computed fixes: The carried-fix rule only catches a fix that repeats an earlier answer exactly. If the first lookup after arriving at a new place returns a newly computed position for the previous place, nothing in the row tells it apart from a real reading. Such events stay in the evidence; they are usually single events, so support counting in device-days keeps them out of supported clusters.
  • SSID semantics: SSIDs are user-set. Name matching is a tie-breaker and Track 3 evidence only.
  • Score double-count: S_bssid and S_depth both reward active days. Kept unchanged pending calibration.
  • Country-wide pin offsets: Each facility is compared with its own pin. If a whole registry is shifted, for example by a datum or projection error, every facility moves into the same distance band and the method reports many individual CAMPUS_DISPERSION or GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH flags instead of one registry-level problem. The Research Log records one such case.

docs.title: 10. Validation
docs.text:
Each version is validated before it is frozen:

  1. Replay the previous and the current version on the same country ledger and publish the flag transition matrix.
  2. Check the Worked Examples against the measured outputs of the current version.
  3. Check every facility of several country ledgers against the Track 1 and action rules, and hand-review a random sample from each flag.
  4. Report how many BSSIDs lose their mobility tag after carried fixes are excluded.

The replay is run with scripts/replay_versions.py, which runs both versions on the same ledger in separate processes and writes the comparison report. The v0.3 results are in the Research Log.

docs.title: Pillar 4: Outage Classification, Connectivity Modeling & 4-State Telemetry
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Determining whether an entity is "online" or "offline" is a non-trivial challenge. A missing telemetry record or failed ping does not automatically indicate an Internet Service Provider (ISP) network blackout.

Real-world deployment environments introduce significant non-network variables:

  1. Facility Operational Schedules: Schools and public facilities close at night and on weekends; hardware is powered off.

  2. Power Grid Instability: Local power grids experience blackouts, shutting down both client hardware and local routers simultaneously.

  3. Offline Sync & Caching Engine: The GigaMeter application utilizes local browser storage (IndexedDB) to cache telemetry offline during outages:

    • Ping Telemetry: Written to IndexedDB immediately upon generation and synced to the server via a background job every 2 hours.
    • Active Speedtests: Measurement payloads are cached locally and synced automatically once connectivity is re-established (retaining up to 7 days of history).
    • Data Retention Rules: Local synced telemetry rows are pruned after 3 days, while un-synced historical data is purged after 30 days.

Pillar 4 exists to establish a rigorous, deterministic baseline for entity connectivity during active operational hours (08:00–19:59 local device time) and serve as the foundation for predictive modeling and automated disconnection alarms.

docs.title: 2. Deterministic Starting Baseline: The 4-State Taxonomy
docs.text:
Time-series ping telemetry (generated every 15 minutes during operational hours) is deterministically categorized into four analytical states:

State Status Name Logical Database Conditions Analytical Interpretation & Real-World Context Metric Impact State A Internet ON is_connected = TRUEAND latency is numerical Client device active, app container functional, end-to-end network reachability validated. Uptime Numerator & Denominator State B Internet OFF is_connected = FALSE Client active, WAN reachability explicitly failed. (Cached in IndexedDB locally; may sync up to 2 hours late). Downtime Denominator State D Degraded / Discrepancy is_connected = TRUEAND latency IS NULL Widespread global pattern (~6.50% of dataset): Connection check succeeds, but latency returns null (severe packet loss or async promise boundary timeout). Awaiting final engineering clarification; isolated in sensitivity models. Isolate / Examine Separately State C Gap / No Observation Missing row inside active operational interval No telemetry received. Indicates hardware powered off, deep sleep, app crash, power cut, or pending sync. Exclude from Uptime Baseline

docs.title: Formal Baseline Uptime Formula:
docs.text:
\[\text{Uptime } (\%) = \frac{\text{Count(State A)}}{\text{Count(State A)} + \text{Count(State B)}} \times 100\]

(Bounded strictly between 08:00 and 19:59 local device time; excludes State C gaps; isolates State D for sensitivity analysis).

docs.title: 3. Future Research & Modeling Roadmap
docs.text:
While the 4-State taxonomy provides the immediate deterministic starting point, Pillar 4 encompasses two upcoming research tracks:

  1. Measurement-Ping Validation Pipeline:

    • Construct an automated cross-validation engine that checks whether active speedtest measurement payloads exist during timeframes where ping telemetry reports downtime (State B) or gaps (State C).
    • Cross-reference startup speedtest runs (trigger_type = 'startup') upon system reboot to verify whether time-series gaps were caused by power restarts vs. ISP outages.

  2. Predictive Time-Series Disconnection Modeling:

    • Build time-series machine learning models to forecast future school offline events and predict imminent disconnections based on historical ping latency jitter, error trends, and regional outage patterns.

docs.title: Pillar 5: ISP SLA Accountability, BBR & Bufferbloat Analytics (Early Stage)
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Standard throughput tests (download and upload speed in Mbps) fail to capture the full quality of service (QoS) experienced by end users. A school may subscribe to a 50 Mbps connection yet suffer unviable performance during digital learning sessions due to high latency under load (Bufferbloat), severe packet loss, or poor backhaul routing.

Pillar 5 exists as an exploratory research pillar to leverage kernel-level NDT7 diagnostic payloads (results JSON) to establish objective ISP Service Level Agreement (SLA) accountability.

docs.title: 2. Exploratory Research Scope & NDT7 Metrics
docs.text:
While Pillar 5 is currently in an early analytical stage, the platform extracts and maps key TCP kernel diagnostic parameters from active NDT7 test runs:

docs.title: 3. Future Analytical Direction
docs.text:
As additional diagnostic dataset assets are integrated into GigaMeter, Pillar 5 research will focus on:

  • Root-Cause Degradation Separation: Isolating whether poor user performance stems from weak local school Wi-Fi signal (wifi_signal_dbm) versus ISP backhaul congestion or inefficient M-Lab server routing.

  • Automated SLA Breach Reporting: Generating automated compliance reports comparing contractual ISP bandwidth and latency guarantees against empirical NDT7 kernel metrics.

docs.title: Worked Examples: Hard-to-Call Facilities
docs.text:
These examples show where a version of the methodology struggled and how the next version responds. They are illustrations, not rules. Each output is labelled with the methodology version that produced it, and the outputs will change as the method changes.

Identifiers, network names, MAC addresses, and coordinates are removed. Distances are rounded. The method changes these examples led to are summarised in the Research Log.

How these outputs were produced

Both columns are measured: each version's code was replayed on the same country ledger (summer 2026, about 9,200 rows from 245 devices).

docs.title: Example A: One Fixed Router, Short Window
docs.text:
Telemetry: One device, one associated router, 7 rows over 3 days. Six rows sit within a few metres of each other. The first reading after start-up lands about 400 m away.

Registry: The official pin is about 15 km from the cluster.

v0.2 v0.3 Device class HIGH_MOBILITY (6/7 rows inside the geofence, below 90%) STATIONARY (one supported cluster, one noise event) Track 1 MINOR_DISCREPANCY, score 53.7 GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH, score 62.7, MEDIUM, FIELD_VERIFY Track 2 no tags no tags Track 3 — UNRESOLVED (network name does not reference the facility)

Why it is hard: The device is clearly stationary, but a single device on a residential-style network cannot show whether it sits in the facility or somewhere else. The pin may be wrong, or the device may be installed elsewhere.

docs.title: Example B: Mostly Wired, One Off-Site Day
docs.text:
Telemetry: One device over seven weeks. About two thirds of rows have no associated Wi-Fi (wired or unassociated). The remainder use a network whose name matches the registered facility name. On one day the device appears about 90 km away on a residential network.

Registry: The official pin is about 17 km from the main cluster.

v0.2 v0.3 Facility centroid Average of all rows, dragged toward the off-site day; about 38 km from the pin Main cluster only; about 17 km from the pin Device class HIGH_MOBILITY (0% compliance against the dragged centroid) STATIONARY (off-site day is unsupported noise) Track 1 MINOR_DISCREPANCY, score 57.5 GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH, score 77.5, HIGH, FIELD_VERIFY Track 2 BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT no split (only one supported cluster) Track 3 — CONSISTENT (network name matches the registry name)

Why it is hard: The first reading suggests the device is at a different facility. The network name instead points to a registry pin that is far off. v0.2 hid a 38 km offset under its mildest flag.

Mean accuracy in the cluster is about 130 m, so the precision factor scores 0. Fifteen days from one stationary device still put the anchor in the HIGH tier. The action stays FIELD_VERIFY because a correction needs at least two devices.

docs.title: Example C: Commuter Laptop Over a School Holiday
docs.text:
Telemetry: One laptop over ten weeks. On school days early in the window it connects to a network named after the facility, about 300 m from the official pin. It also uses two home networks about 3 km away. After the term ends it stays at home. In many rows the coordinates are copied from the previous row even though the associated network changed.

v0.2 v0.3 Hotspot tagging 100% of rows tagged, because carried coordinates made both fixed routers look as if they moved About 2% of fix events tagged, the genuine phone-hotspot events Facility centroid Facility network's rows mixed both locations; centroid about 1.9 km from the pin Govt proximity picks the facility cluster (about 300 m from the pin); telemetry dominance picks the home cluster (about 3.4 km) Device class COMMUTER COMMUTER Track 1 GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH, score 75.8 Strategies disagree; the registry name match picks the facility cluster: CAMPUS_DISPERSION (about 300 m), score 69.3, MEDIUM, FIELD_VERIFY, anchor_resolved_by = ssid_name_match Track 2 HOTSPOT_TETHERED_FACILITY BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT (home and facility clusters are both supported, about 3.2 km apart), COMMUTER_DEVICE Track 3 — CONSISTENT

Why it is hard: By volume, the home is the dominant location because the window spans a holiday. Without the name match the honest answer is AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER. A term calendar is not modelled in v0.3.

docs.title: Pillar 1: Entity Geofencing & Mobility Trajectory Detection
docs.text:
v0.3

This page describes the v0.3 methodology, which the MobilityAnalyzer code implements. Settings are on the Parameters page.

docs.title: 1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
In crowdsourced field telemetry, client monitoring software (the GigaMeter application) runs on hardware devices - such as laptops, tablets, desktop PCs, or smartphones - that are inherently susceptible to physical movement.

In real-world deployment scenarios:

  • Teachers or school staff frequently take laptops home during off-hours or weekends.

  • Hardware equipment is occasionally transferred between facilities or regional offices.

  • Users run speedtests while connected to mobile hotspots or in transit.

If telemetry from a roaming laptop is blindly assigned to a static school facility, speedtest results recorded at a teacher's home 50 kilometers away will pollute the connectivity baseline of the school building. Pillar 1 evaluates hardware movement at the individual device level, separating fixed facility anchors from mobile or commuting hardware.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Isolate Device Trajectories: Track individual hardware instances (device_id / browser_id) across time and space using DBSCAN on fix events.

  • Classify Without a Facility Prior: A device is classified from its own clusters and dates. It does not depend on the facility centroid, so a wrong centroid cannot make every device look mobile.

  • Separate Class From Evidence: Every device reports a mobility class and, separately, evidence_device_days.

  • Classify Hardware Mobility Taxonomy:

    1. STATIONARY: One supported cluster with a low noise share.

    2. COMMUTER: Two or more supported clusters, with the device switching between them at least commuter_min_alternations times.

    3. RELOCATED: Two or more supported clusters with fewer switches, meaning the device moved and stayed.

    4. HIGH_MOBILITY: Enough evidence, but no supported cluster, or too much noise.

    5. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: Too few fix events, or fix events on a single day, so no cluster could be supported. Checked first, so a device seen once is not called mobile.

docs.title: 3. Key Analytical Mechanics
docs.text:
• Fix Events: Rows are collapsed into fix events. Carried fixes (coordinates repeated under a different network) are excluded. See Blueprint Section 2.

  • DBSCAN Clustering: Haversine DBSCAN on fix events with device_eps_m and device_min_samples.

  • Supported Clusters: A cluster counts only when it spans at least min_cluster_device_days days. Single-day excursions become noise.

  • Dominant Cluster: The cluster with the most support. Cluster labels such as 0 carry no meaning.

  • Geofence Audit: Each device's displacement from a reference point is reported as an audit and never feeds classification. The reference is the facility anchor (Pillar 2) when known, otherwise the device's dominant cluster; reference_source says which. See Blueprint Section 4.3.

docs.title: Pillar 2: Geolocation Quality, BSSID Fingerprinting & Confidence Scoring
docs.text:
v0.3

This page describes the v0.3 methodology. SpatialProfiler implements the anchor selection and FacilityValidator the scores. Settings are on the Parameters page.

docs.title: 1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Crowdsourced Wi-Fi location resolution depends on environmental scans submitted to Google's Geolocation API. Field environments present significant spatial noise:

  • Facilities in rural areas may scan only 1 or 2 nearby Wi-Fi routers, yielding lower precision radii.

  • Staff frequently use consumer mobile hotspots (e.g., "iPhone", "Galaxy A15"), which move across days.

  • Devices are carried between the facility and other places, so one facility's telemetry can describe several locations.

  • Consecutive rows often repeat the same coordinates, sometimes under a different network than the one that produced them.

GigaMeter operates under a Strict No-IP Policy. If Wi-Fi geolocation fails, coordinates stay NULL. Pillar 2 selects the observed location that represents the facility, quantifies confidence in it (0–100), and detects mobile tethering.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Fix Events as Evidence: Count support in fix events and device-days, never raw rows.

  • BSSID Mobility Detection: Flag a network as mobile when its own accurate, non-carried fixes form two or more supported clusters.

  • Facility Observation Clusters: Cluster all anchor-window fix events, including events without a BSSID, and select exactly one cluster as the facility anchor.

  • No Averaging Across Clusters: A facility coordinate is always computed inside one cluster.

  • Strategy Agreement: Run govt proximity and telemetry dominance, report whether they agree, and resolve disagreement only by a registry name match.

  • BSSID Coherence Penalty (P_coherence): Scale down hardware health when supported clusters are far apart.

docs.title: 3. Key Analytical Mechanics
docs.text:
• Accuracy-Weighted Centroid (one weight per fix event, inside the anchor cluster):
\[w_i = \frac{1}{\max(A_i, A_{\text{floor}})^2}\] \[\bar{\phi} = \frac{\sum (w_i \cdot \phi_i)}{\sum w_i}, \quad \bar{\lambda} = \frac{\sum (w_i \cdot \lambda_i)}{\sum w_i}\]
  • 5-Factor Composite Score (S_raw, 0–100), computed on the anchor cluster:
\[S_{\text{raw}} = \underbrace{S_{\text{stability}}}_{\text{30 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{consensus}}}_{\text{25 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{bssid}}}_{\text{20 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{depth}}}_{\text{15 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{precision}}}_{\text{10 pt}}\]
  • Coherence Multiplier (P_coherence), where \(D_{\text{split}}\) is the maximum distance between supported facility clusters:
\[P_{\text{coherence}} = \begin{cases} 1.0, & \text{if } D_{\text{split}} \le 1000\text{m} \\[1ex] 1.0 - 0.5 \times \left( \frac{D_{\text{split}} - 1000}{1000} \right), & \text{if } 1000\text{m} < D_{\text{split}} \le 2000\text{m} \\[1ex] 0.1, & \text{if } D_{\text{split}} > 2000\text{m} \end{cases}\]

Full rules are in Blueprint Section 5.

docs.title: Pillar 3: Government Data Validation & Administrative Map Auditing
docs.text:
v0.3

This page describes the v0.3 methodology, which the FacilityValidator code implements. Settings are on the Parameters page.

docs.title: 1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
National Ministries of Education and telecommunications authorities maintain registries with official coordinates for public schools and health centers. These registries often contain legacy mapping errors:

  • School pins are placed at the center of a village, district office, or capital city rather than on the building.
  • New or relocated facilities are registered with estimated coordinates.

Telemetry can also be misleading: a device may be installed at a home or at another facility. Pillar 3 therefore asks two questions separately: does the government pin match where the telemetry is (Track 1), and is that telemetry attributable to this entity (Track 3)? Hardware reliability (Track 2) never hides either answer.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Empirical Displacement: Haversine distance (D_govt) between the anchor centroid and the official pin, always reported when both exist.
  • Multi-Track Decoupling:
    • Track 1 (Location Truth): Distance-band flag plus a separate confidence tier and recommended action.
    • Track 2 (Hardware Integrity): S_raw x P_coherence and hardware anomaly tags.
    • Track 3 (Entity Attribution): Registry name match and nearest other registered entity.
  • Track 1 Flags:
    • VERIFIED_ACCURATE: Anchor within verified_max_m of the pin.
    • CAMPUS_DISPERSION: Between verified_max_m and mismatch_min_m.
    • GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH: Beyond mismatch_min_m.
    • AMBIGUOUS_MULTI_CLUSTER: Strategies chose different clusters and no name match resolves them.
    • UNSTABLE_MOBILE_ONLY: No supported anchor cluster.
    • NO_GOVT_PIN_AVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
  • Recommended Actions: SUBMIT_CORRECTION only for high-confidence mismatches seen by two or more devices; NONE for verified pins; AWAIT_DATA for low confidence or too little data; FIELD_VERIFY for everything else, including ambiguous and single-device results. The ordered rules are in Blueprint Section 6.2.
  • Track 3 Pins: The country table of official pins is loaded from Delta Sharing so that pins of facilities without telemetry are also checked.
